name: Town of Mount Pleasant (unincorporated)
gaps: The schedule sets no maximum floor area / FAR and no impervious or total coverage limit for residence districts; only building coverage and a minimum floor area per dwelling.
R-5A and R-3A entries hold the one-family (Same as R-10) standards; multifamily standards are in notes.
Lot width recorded is width at the front-yard setback line; mean width is in notes. No separate frontage requirement in the schedule.
R-40/R-20 shed setbacks: § 218-13D and § 218-20.3 say 10 ft from side/rear lines, but § 218-20.3 defers to the schedule when stricter (R-40 schedule = same as main building).
PRD-T-5 total side yard is printed as 50 ft (same as the one-side minimum) with a footnote; recorded as printed.
Hamlet districts (HH, HHC, TH, VH; § 218-68.1) and PRD-T-8 (not in the county layer) were not researched for one-family rules.
Supplement dates on attachments run 2006-2023; Mount Pleasant eCode360 may lag recent local laws.

wetlands.summary: Ch. 111: in mapped Wetlands Control Districts, no building, filling or removal of material within 50 ft of a wetland, water body or watercourse without Town Engineer or Planning Board approval.

steep_slopes.summary: Ch. 180: permit for new buildings, additions, clearing, grading or stormwater work on slopes of 15%+ (area >= 500 sf); Town Engineer for 15-25%, Planning Board with public hearing for 25%+. Hilltop/ridgeline work is a SEQRA Type I action.

trees.summary: Ch. 201: Town Arborist permit to remove or disturb trees on streets or Town property; on private land the tree-preservation standards (specimen trees 30 in. hardwood / 36 in. softwood / 12 in. small DBH) apply to development applications, including new one- and two-family houses.

stormwater.summary: Ch. 183: stormwater review and SWPPP for land development activity disturbing 1 acre or more (or part of a larger common plan).

adu.summary: § 218-36: one accessory apartment per one-family lot by Planning Board permit, owner-occupied, inside a principal dwelling at least 10 years old, max 25% of the dwelling or 600 sf (100 sf waiver possible).

general.accessory_structures: § 218-13: attached accessory buildings follow main-building rules; detached ones too, except those <= 15 ft / 1 story may use the schedule's accessory columns (R-10: 5 ft side/rear; R-20: 10/25 ft; R-40: same as main) if behind the front setback line, and must be 25 ft from the main building unless the schedule says otherwise. Sheds: § 218-20.3.
general.pools: Fenced private pools are permitted accessory uses; the schedule header requires accessory uses to meet principal-building rules (no separate pool setback found in Ch. 218).
general.notes: Fences max 4 ft in front/side yards and 6 ft in rear yards (6 ft anywhere in R-40) (§ 218-12F). Corner-lot sight triangle 30 ft (§ 218-14).

R-40.name: R-40 One-Family Residential

accessory.notes: Detached accessory buildings <= 15 ft / 1 story: same side and rear distances as main buildings, 20 ft from the main building, behind the front setback line (cols 13-15; § 218-13B). Sheds max 15 ft high, rear yard; § 218-13D and § 218-20.3 say 10 ft from side/rear lines but defer to the schedule where it is more restrictive.

R-40.source: § 218-10 Schedule of Regulations, Residence Districts I (Attachment 1)
R-40.notes: Lot width = width at front-yard setback line (mean width 150 ft, mean depth 175 ft). On streets under 50 ft wide the front yard is measured from the street center line plus 25 ft; corner lots need a front yard on each street and a rear yard (col 23). Minimum floor area 1,000 sf on one floor or 1,200 sf on two floors.

R-20.name: R-20 One-Family Residential

accessory.notes: Detached accessory buildings <= 15 ft / 1 story: 10 ft from side and 25 ft from rear lot lines, 15 ft from the main building, behind the front setback line (cols 13-15; § 218-13B). Sheds max 12 ft high, rear yard, 25 ft from house (§ 218-20.3).

R-20.source: § 218-10 Schedule of Regulations, Residence Districts I (Attachment 1)
R-20.notes: Lot width = width at front-yard setback line (mean width 100 ft, mean depth 150 ft). Front yard measured from center line plus 25 ft on streets under 50 ft wide; corner lots need a front yard on each street (col 23, same as R-40). Minimum floor area same as R-40.

R-10.name: R-10 One-Family Residential

accessory.notes: Detached accessory buildings <= 15 ft / 1 story: 5 ft from side and rear lot lines, 12 ft from the main building, behind the front setback line (cols 13-15; § 218-13B). Taller ones follow principal rules. Sheds max 12 ft high, rear yard, 5 ft from lot lines (§ 218-20.3).

R-10.source: § 218-10 Schedule of Regulations, Residence Districts III (Attachment 8)
R-10.notes: Lot width = width at front-yard setback line (mean width 75 ft, mean depth 100 ft). On streets under 50 ft wide the front yard is measured from the street center line plus 25 ft; corner lots need a front yard on each street (col 23, same as R-40). Minimum floor area 1,000 sf on one floor or 1,200 sf on two floors.

R-5A.name: R-5A Multifamily Residential

accessory.notes: Detached accessory buildings <= 15 ft / 1 story: 5 ft from side and rear lot lines, 12 ft from the main building, behind the front setback line (cols 13-15; § 218-13B). Taller ones follow principal rules. Sheds max 12 ft high, rear yard, 5 ft from lot lines (§ 218-20.3).

R-5A.source: § 218-10 Schedule of Regulations, Residence Districts III (Attachment 8)
R-5A.notes: Values shown are for one-family and other non-multifamily uses, which the schedule sets as 'Same as R-10'. Multifamily dwellings (1 unit per 5,000 sf, Planning Board site plan, §§ 218-64, 218-65): 10-acre site, width 250 ft, mean width/depth 300 ft, front 75, sides 50 (total 100), rear 75, 2.5 stories / 40 ft, 15% coverage, buildings max 180 ft long.

R-3A.name: R-3A Multifamily Residential

accessory.notes: Detached accessory buildings <= 15 ft / 1 story: 5 ft from side and rear lot lines, 12 ft from the main building, behind the front setback line (cols 13-15; § 218-13B). Taller ones follow principal rules. Sheds max 12 ft high, rear yard, 5 ft from lot lines (§ 218-20.3).

R-3A.source: § 218-10 Schedule of Regulations, Residence Districts III (Attachment 8)
R-3A.notes: Values shown are for one-family and other non-multifamily uses ('Same as R-10' via R-5A). Multifamily dwellings (1 unit per 3,500 sf): 2-acre site, width/mean width/depth 200 ft, front 65, sides 40 (total 80), rear 40, 2.5 stories / 40 ft, 20% coverage.

PRDT-1.name: PRD-T-1 Planned Residential Development, Transitional-1

accessory.notes: Detached accessory buildings: same side/rear distances as the principal building; no minimum distance from the main building (cols 13-15).

PRDT-1.source: § 218-10 Schedule of Regulations, Residence Districts II (Attachment 2); § 218-76
PRDT-1.notes: Site 3 to 5 acres (mean width 200 ft). Uses as in R-5A; Planning Board special permit and conceptual site plan required. Minimum floor area 450 sf per unit.

PRDT-2.name: PRD-T-2 Planned Residential Development, Transitional-2

accessory.notes: Detached accessory buildings: same side/rear distances as the principal building; no minimum distance from the main building (cols 13-15).

PRDT-2.source: § 218-10 Schedule of Regulations, Residence Districts IIA (Attachment 3); § 218-76
PRDT-2.notes: Site 4 to 6 acres; R-5A uses at no more than 1 unit per 8,300 sf of site. 2 stories, or 3 if the Planning Board approves (col 23).

PRDT-5.name: PRD-T-5 Planned Residential Development, Transitional-5

accessory.notes: Detached accessory buildings: same side/rear distances as principal; distance from main building as approved by Planning Board.

PRDT-5.source: § 218-10 Schedule of Regulations, Residence Districts IIC (Attachment 5); § 218-76
PRDT-5.notes: Site 3 to 7 acres. Total-of-two side yards printed as 50 ft with footnote 1: 'Except where 1 side yard is bordered by a 90-foot perpetual buffer conservation area.'

PRDT-6.name: PRD-T-6 Planned Residential Development, Transitional-6 (Quarry/Kensington)

accessory.notes: Detached accessory buildings: same side/rear distances as principal; distance from main building as approved by Planning Board.

PRDT-6.source: § 218-10 Schedule of Regulations, Residence Districts IIC (Attachment 5); § 218-76
PRDT-6.notes: 5,000 sf per dwelling unit; single-ownership lots of 4,500 sf+ at adoption may hold one single-family house. Detached/attached single-family and 2-family homes. Mean width/depth per Planning Board site plan. Corner lots need only one designated front yard (30 ft). Planning Board may cut the rear yard up to 40%. Minimum floor area 750 sf; special permit required.

PRDT-7.name: PRD-T-7 Planned Residential Development, Transitional-7 (Overlook Estates)

accessory.notes: Detached accessory buildings: same side/rear distances as principal; no restriction on distance from main building.

PRDT-7.source: § 218-10 Schedule of Regulations, Residence Districts IID (Attachment 6)
PRDT-7.notes: 2.4-acre site, max 27 units (35 with 5 affordable). Multifamily and 2-family dwellings. Mean width printed as 25 ft. Planning Board may reduce setbacks up to 60% and allow up to 3 stories / 40 ft.

PRDH-T1.name: PRDH-T-1 Planned Residential - Historic Development, Transitional

accessory.notes: Detached accessory buildings: same as main building; no restriction on distance from main building.

PRDH-T1.source: § 218-10 Schedule of Regulations, Residence Districts IIB (Attachment 4); Residence Districts III (Attachment 8) for R-10 yards
PRDH-T1.notes: 6-acre site (Troop K barracks), width 600 ft, mean width 300 ft, mean depth 500 ft. Yards are 'Same as R-10' (values from the R-10 row). Planning Board may reduce yards up to 60% (not below facing building height). Density R-10 base, up to 1 unit per 5,000 sf (max 56 units) by special permit.
